name: SIGINT
standfirst: Security research and practitioner news, scored for novelty and actionability.
colophon: sigint.wtf — the correct response to most of these CVEs. Scored by machine against a hand-written rubric; ranking is opinion, not fact.

items.title: From Reactive Containment to Proactive Assurance: Lessons from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google Agent Security Incidents
items.dek: Agent eval escapes (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google) show boundaries fail under test; proposes Boundary Assurance Stack for runtime verification.
items.unproven: Framework not yet deployed in live agent systems; cases are post-hoc analysis, not prospective validation of the PASAC model.

items.title: Provable Subexponential Algorithms for NIST Third-Round Lattice Families
items.dek: Subexponential lattice algorithms break Kyber, FrodoKEM, SABER, NTRU, and Dilithium with polylogarithmic coefficient scales; initiate migration planning immediately.
items.unproven: whether NIST parameter choices fall within vulnerable regime; classical-only, no quantum speedup analysis; migration timeline and cryptanalytic feasibility against deployed hardened implementations unclear.

items.title: Skill Constellations: Tracing the Supply Chain of Agent Skills on GitHub
items.dek: 14.9% of high-risk agent skill adoptions prevented by auditing top-100 source repositories ranked by copy network, versus 0.5% for most-starred.
items.unproven: whether ranking generalizes as new skills enter ecosystem; limited to GitSkills dataset; assumes reader has visibility into SKILL.md supply chain in current SDLC.

items.title: CVE-2016-3081 — Apache Struts Command Injection Vulnerability
items.dek: Apache Struts. Confirmed exploited in the wild. Federal remediation due 11 October.

items.title: CVE-2023-22894 — Strapi Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information Vulnerability
items.dek: Strapi Strapi. Confirmed exploited in the wild. Federal remediation due 11 October.

items.title: CVE-2021-3199 — ONLYOFFICE Docs Server Path Traversal Vulnerability
items.dek: ONLYOFFICE Docs. Confirmed exploited in the wild. Federal remediation due 11 October.

items.title: CVE-2015-3306 — ProFTPD Improper Access Control Vulnerability
items.dek: ProFTPD ProFTPD. Confirmed exploited in the wild. Federal remediation due 11 October.

items.title: CVE-2015-5477 — ISC BIND Data Processing Errors Vulnerability
items.dek: ISC BIND. Confirmed exploited in the wild. Federal remediation due 11 October.

items.title: Design-Time Conformance Checking for Pulse-Level Quantum Control
items.dek: Design-time pulse conformance checker validates quantum control programs against versioned device capability descriptors before execution.
items.unproven: Evaluated against two vendor toolchains; generalization to emerging vendors and heterogeneous device clusters not established.

items.title: Constrained-Action AI Remediation for SIEM/XDR via a NeMo-Guardrails Proxy
items.dek: Constrained-action LLM architecture for SOC/XDR remediation with NeMo-Guardrails proxy lifts injection detection from 25% to 94.5%.
items.unproven: Evaluation on synthetic corpus and limited red-team exercise; production SOC deployment and long-term robustness not demonstrated.

items.title: Package Hallucination Attacks on Coding Agents through Prompt Injection in Rule Files
items.dek: Coding agents can be tricked via malicious .cursorrules prompts to swap legitimate dependencies for attacker packages at high success rates.
items.unproven: Attack success measured on benchmarks and sandbox environments; requires attacker write access to rule files before agent execution.

items.title: Cost of Delay for Post-Quantum Migration: Putting Classical and Harvest-Now-Decrypt-Later Risk on One Ordered List
items.dek: Post-quantum migration cost-of-delay model unifies harvest-now-decrypt-later and classical risk in annualized currency to sequence asset migration.
items.unproven: Quantum-arrival law calibrated to published expert anchors, not empirical intercept rates; assumes recordable traffic share is known and stable.

items.title: Multi-Aspect Runtime Verification for Simulation-Based V&V of LLM-Enabled Autonomous Agents
items.dek: Runtime verification framework decomposes LLM-agent policy obligations into spatial, temporal, and semantic aspects to catch multi-step tool chains that per-event guardrails miss.
items.unproven: whether the four-valued algebra scales to large policy sets; validation on real defense-domain agents; whether spatial and temporal specifications generalize to policies outside the defense context described.

items.title: False Claims, Credible Images: A Red-Teaming Benchmark for Commercial Image Generators
items.dek: Commercial image generators produce credible-looking visual misinformation despite recognizing claims as false; 10k-prompt benchmark exposes misalignment in safeguards.
items.unproven: whether defenses scale beyond benchmark; limited to open-ended prompts; no evidence of widespread exploitation in supply chains or SDLC contexts.

items.title: Standard estimators cannot represent fault-tolerant workloads at measured error rates: evaluated, evidence-based uncertainty for quantum resource estimation
items.dek: Propagating actual measured error rates through five cost models widens RSA-2048 qubit estimates 40× and raises median 4.6× above conventional point estimates.
items.unproven: Post-quantum migration timeline assumes surface-code surface-code architecture; applicability across competing qubit modalities and competing error-correction codes not evaluated.

items.title: On the Reliability of LLM-Based Vulnerability Patching Benchmarks
items.dek: LLM patch benchmarks systematically overstate performance through prompting, infrastructure, and dataset artifacts; 112-bug benchmark with regression tests corrects this.
items.unproven: limited to C/C++, Go, Rust; applicability to high-level languages and non-memory-safety domains not demonstrated

items.title: Sensitive-Topic Leakage Through LLM Routing Metadata: Measurement and Mitigation
items.dek: LLM router choice metadata leaks sensitive request topics; real-world measurement on 1.7M requests with tested mitigations.
items.unproven: Limited to two routers and one dataset; generalization to other routing architectures and model families not established.

items.title: Hybrid Hierarchical Runtime Verification for Edge-IoT Security: Combining MonPoly and RTLola
items.dek: Three-layer runtime verification combining MonPoly and RTLola detects coordinated edge-IoT attacks and silent-node persistence.
items.unproven: Evaluation limited to 15-node Docker testbed; scalability to production edge-IoT fleets and protocol-independent attacks unclear.

items.title: Automotive Hardware Attacks: An Architect's Guide to TARA
items.dek: Extended TARA framework for automotive hardware attacks adds evidence gates and attack-potential dominance to ISO/SAE 21434.
items.unproven: adoption by automotive architects or whether the three-level gate proves workable in practice across supplier chains

items.title: Secure-CUA: Controlling Untrusted Influence in Computer-Use Agents
items.dek: Formalized security model for computer-use agents that commits to action programs before accessing untrusted GUI content.
items.unproven: No evaluation on agents deployed in production SDLC pipelines; threat model does not address side-channel leaks through timing or resource observation.

items.title: Adversarial Images Hijack Web Agents from Visual Grounding to Browser Execution
items.dek: Adversarial images crafted to persist through vision-language grounding cause web agents to select and execute attacker-controlled actions on real websites.
items.unproven: Tested on public websites with static renderings; real-world adaptive defenses and image compression in transit not evaluated.

items.title: How Fragile Is On-Device Language Model Safety? Localizing Safety-Critical Parameters for Sparse Fault Analysis
items.dek: Modifying 0.19% of LLaMA-2-7B parameters in specific layers triggers 53% jailbreak success, suggesting on-device models need targeted integrity protection.
items.unproven: whether other model families show the same parameter concentration; whether this holds across different quantization schemes or in actual deployed on-device settings; transferability to larger or smaller models.

items.title: I think we might lose public key cryptography
items.dek: Post-quantum cryptography timeline concerns; informs migration planning but offers no new technical findings.
items.unproven: no quantified threat calendar or migration path beyond speculation

items.title: HPQ-AKE: A Provably Secure Sign-Less Hybrid Authenticated Key Exchange Protocol for Bandwidth-Constrained IoT and Edge Networks
items.dek: HPQ-AKE replaces post-quantum signatures with dual KEMs for IoT handshakes; reduces bandwidth 57%, proven secure in extended BR model.
items.unproven: Analytical model and simulation only; no hardware or firmware deployment data; RSA infrastructure assumption may not hold for all IoT gateways; reader's org likely preparing PQC migration planning, but implementation is GRC-level, not SDLC-integrated.

items.title: From Public Posts to AI-Search Citations: Measuring the Fragility of AI Search
items.dek: Measurement framework reveals low-barrier publication domains can become indirect citation paths into AI-search answers across 10 platforms.
items.unproven: attack feasibility and real-world exploitation likelihood; whether platforms adjust citation selection post-disclosure.

noise.title: Strands Decider 2B: a small, open-source, decision model
noise.dek: Small decision-making model released open-source; relevant as agents enter SDLC but requires testing in reader's own environment.
noise.unproven: suitability for financial services workloads, behavior under adversarial input, governance implications in production SDLC

noise.title: Penguin Mail – open-source Rust email client for Linux with AI
noise.dek: Linux email client written in Rust with AI features; product launch with no security or process implications for AppSec teams.

noise.title: Incident with Git Operations, Pull Requests and Actions – Resolved
noise.dek: GitHub platform incident affecting Git operations and Actions resolved; status report only, no new vulnerability or configuration change required.
